items.title: LLMs corrupt your documents when you delegate
items.summary: A study introducing DELEGATE-52 evaluates LLM readiness for delegated workflows requiring in-depth document editing. It finds that even frontier models corrupt an average of 25% of document content in long workflows, with degradation worsening with document size and interaction length. The research concludes that current LLMs are unreliable delegates, introducing sparse but severe errors that silently corrupt documents over time.

items.title: Can LLMs model real-world systems in TLA+?
items.summary: The Specula team developed SysMoBench, an automated benchmark, to evaluate LLMs' ability to model real-world systems in TLA+. They found that while LLMs produce syntactically correct and runnable TLA+ specs, they struggle with accurately reflecting system semantics, often generating "textbook models" that diverge from actual system behavior. Leading LLMs achieved low scores (around 46% conformance, 41% invariant) because their models either entered states real systems couldn't reach or failed to reach states real systems always reached.

items.title: Show HN: Git for AI Agents
items.summary: re_gent is a new version control system designed specifically for AI agent activity, tracking agent actions, associated prompts, and file changes. It allows developers to log agent activity, blame specific lines of code on agent steps, and rewind to previous states, aiming to improve debugging and auditability for agent-driven development. The tool integrates with agents like Claude and provides command-line utilities and a VS Code extension for inline blame and session history.
